title: Isolated Deploy POC - Checklist & Field Questions
summary: Working notes and field checklist for an isolated (air-gapped / no-internet) on-prem POC. Focus is rapid feasibility assessment during a 2-hour customer workshop + inventory capture for a follow-up runbook.
context: Customer: mid-market healthtech, needs private deployment for PHI workloads. They have an internal platform team, limited cloud footprint for regulated workloads, and want to validate a minimal Redwood Private POC in an isolated datacenter cage. This doc captures the questions we should ask during the initial site discovery and lists constraints likely to block a quick POC.
poc_goals: 1) Stand up a minimal inference cluster reachable from the customer's internal app servers. 2) Validate model serving latency at target QPS with KV cache behavior. 3) Prove secure artifact delivery and offline upgrades. 4) Demonstrate telemetry upload via outbound proxy (or confirm alternate).
minimal_hardware_suggestion: Recommend starting with a 2-node GPU cluster: each node 2 x NVIDIA A10/A100 (or equivalent), 256GB RAM, 2 x 1.6TB NVMe for OS+model cache, 2 x 10Gb NICs. If budget allows, 4x A10 across 2 nodes gives better headroom. Include a dedicated management VM for control plane components.
hardware_checks:
- Rack U available and labelled
- Power PDUs and per-rack capacity (amps)
- Redundant power feed? (yes/no)
- Available GPUs (model + firmware) and current driver install
- BIOS/firmware access for updates
- Hardware vendor support SLA
- Local NVRAM/TPM presence (for attestation)
- Serial console access or IPMI/BMC reachable from admin VLAN
network_requirements:
- Is the environment fully air-gapped (no egress) or strictly restricted?
- Allowed outbound hosts/ports if any (egress allowlist)
- Proxy details (IP, port, auth type, TLS interception)
- DNS policy (internal-only? split-horizon?)
- Internal load balancer availability or ability to configure VIPs
- VLANs available for mgmt/data/telemetry separation
- MTU considerations for NVMe-over-fabrics (if used)
- Firewall change process and lead time
security_requirements:
- Customer KMS strategy: do they allow external keys or must we integrate with on-prem HSM/KMS?
- Requirements for network isolation and RBAC mapping to their IdP (SAML/Okta)
- Audit/log retention requirements and where logs must be shipped (SIEM/ELK on-prem)
- Mandatory compliance attestations (SOC2, HIPAA controls they enforce locally)
- Container signing and image provenance expectations
- Requirements for FIPS/Crypto modules
operational_constraints:
- No internet: how do we deliver container images/artifacts? (option: signed tarball + checksum + offline installer)
- Allowed maintenance windows and change freeze periods
- Support channel & on-call escalation: who on customer side has physical access?
- Backup/restore expectations and acceptable RTO/RPO for model artifacts
- How are patches accepted? automatic via USB or manual approved process?
common_blockers_seen_in_field:
- NVIDIA driver/OS mismatch preventing GPU utilization
- Locked-down bastions that block necessary ports (gRPC/metrics)
- Lack of spare rack space or insufficient power headroom
- Security team refusal to accept remote assistance or shell access
- No workable way to transfer large model artifacts (tens-hundreds GB) into the environment
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: customer cannot allow any outbound telemetry. Mitigation: show local-only logging and provide an optional snapshot export process.
- Risk: GPU drivers incompatible with Redwood runtime. Mitigation: bring prebuilt driver+runtime bundle and validation steps; require vendor drivers be staged.
- Risk: Extended firewall change lead times. Mitigation: propose an offline test plan that uses temporary physical access or pre-approved IP ranges.
field_questions:
(To use verbatim in workshop)
1) Can you confirm the exact network path from app tier to the proposed inference rack? Any known middleboxes?
2) Are there corporate policies around removable media / USB we should be aware of?
3) Who owns the rack network ACLs and what is SLA for rule changes?
4) Do you have a secure file transfer process for multi-GB artifacts today?
5) Is there a preferred HSM/KMS vendor and process for key rotation?
6) Will we have a local account with sudo and IPMI access for the duration of the POC?
7) Can we schedule a 30–60 minute window with your security engineer to review TLS/PKI expectations?
open_questions:
- Does the customer require signed hardware attestation (TPM) for every node?
- Can the control plane (operator) be hosted outside the air-gapped network under a VPN, or must it be fully on-prem?
- Are there restrictions on container runtimes (docker vs containerd)?
- Who approves temporary firewall exceptions if we need to fetch a hotfix?
- Acceptable method for telemetry: outbound to vendor-managed collector, push to SFTP, or entirely manual export?
next_steps:
- Book 2-hour site discovery workshop with infra + security + platform (send invite with pre-read).
- Send inventory template to customer: rack IDs, PDU details, NIC part numbers, GPU model+firmware, BMC access.
- Prepare offline delivery artifact: signed image tarball, install checklist, validation notebook.
- Draft a one-page POC runbook with rollback steps and escalation contacts.
- Follow up: internal pre-call with SE team 48h before workshop.
notes_to_self:
- Bring a USB with signed image, but also prepare encrypted external disk if they permit it.
- Keep checklist printed for field visit; collect screenshots of IPMI and dmesg on first boot.
- If driver problems occur, spin up a local containerized repro to capture logs before requesting vendor support.
